solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ridicule dogs histrionic performer in bed?

indicators.note: to dog someone is to follow close behind them, so one piece trails straight after the other

blocks.note: a ham is an actor who overplays every scene
to ridicule is to mock

explanation.surface: Scorn pursues a hammy actor even as he lies in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads Ridicule first, but 'dogs' means it trails behind, so the actor comes first. The question mark flags that a hanging net is only loosely a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinging net or canvas sling strung between posts is used for sleeping, so it serves as a kind of bed.

clue.text: Play along with setters, reportedly supplying bone

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: to humour someone is to play along with them, and 'us' stands for the setters

explanation.surface: A performer plays along with the puzzle compilers, as if putting on a show for them.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'us' or 'me' in clues; here 'setters' is the plural we. HUMOUR US spoken aloud matches the bone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The long upper-arm skeleton piece running from shoulder to elbow is a bone, the one behind the 'funny bone' joke.

clue.text: Alternative names for minute undergarments without opening

indicators.note: lacking its opening means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time
knickers are women's underpants, the British everyday word

explanation.surface: Someone lists the other names people use for tiny underwear, with a slightly saucy air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like 'tiny' describing the underwear, but it is the noun, a short time. Dropping the silent K leaves NICKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A moniker is an informal name or nickname, so monickers are the other labels someone goes by besides their real one.

clue.text: Old church overlooking an expanse of water

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking means sitting above, so the earlier pieces stack on top of the next

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient chapel stands on a cliff looking out over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a seaside view, but 'an expanse of water' splits: 'an' is used as letters and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The great body of salt water covering most of the planet is the largest expanse there is.

clue.text: Kane disheartened and upset about France controversy

indicators.note: losing heart means the inner letters go and only the outside pair stays
about means around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
to ruffle someone is to upset them
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Footballer Harry Kane is downcast and upset about a row involving France.
explanation.walkthrough: Kane reads as the England striker, but only his outer letters are used. 'Upset' looks like a second mood word; it is the verb RUFFLE, which goes around F.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a commotion or fuss, an informal word for a public row or dispute stirring strong feelings.

clue.text: People wearing monastic garb

definitions.note: verb: to people a place is to fill it with inhabitants

blocks.note: someone in a coat is wearing it
a habit is the robe worn by a monk or nun

explanation.surface: A group of people dressed in monks' robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb meaning to populate, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To people an area is to live in it or fill it with residents, which is exactly what inhabiting a place involves.

clue.text: Surmise case of Italian match official is over

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell of something, so only the two outside letters are kept
turned over, something is flipped end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
a ref is a referee

explanation.surface: Someone guesses the Italian referee's case is closed and the game finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is over' sounds like the match ending, but it tells you to turn REF round.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmise is to conclude something from the available evidence, which is what inferring means.

clue.text: Uplands bordering Oregon essentially abounding with black birds

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the middle letter is taken
to border something is to run all round its edge, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: uplands are hilly country
OR is the US postal abbreviation for Oregon
the fifth of nine letters is the centre one
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Hill country along Oregon's borders is teeming with blackbirds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black birds' looks like one phrase, but black gives just B and birds is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornbills are tropical birds of Africa and Asia with huge curved beaks, often topped with a casque.

clue.text: Instrument of justice cop unsheathed pursuing outlaw

indicators.note: taken out of its sheath, a word loses its outer covering and only the inside stays
one thing pursuing another comes behind it, so these pieces go after

blocks.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
J is the abbreviation for Justice, a judge's title
the inner letter of the word

explanation.surface: A policeman drawing a weapon as an instrument of justice chases a bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument of justice' reads as one phrase, like a sword; it splits into the definition, a link and J.
explanation.definitionFit: The banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a round drum-like body, strummed or plucked in folk and bluegrass.

clue.text: Heroic character initially stopped English invading America

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
an invader goes inside another's territory, so these letters are placed within

blocks.note: America is the US, with the article added
the first letter of the word
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A hero at first halts an English invasion of America.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading America with the definite article added is a common crossword trick, and the two short pieces slip between the article and the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the Greek mythological hero who slew the Minotaur in the Cretan labyrinth, a character from legend.

clue.text: Reflecting, say, on chap’s cause of hair loss

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters appear back to front
in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

blocks.note: a chap is a man
e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A man thinking about what is making him go bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflecting' suggests pondering, but it turns EG around; the 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mange is a skin disease of animals caused by mites, making fur fall out in patches.

clue.text: Quotation about barrier around outskirts of Rome

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are used
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a fence is a barrier
the first and last letters of the city

explanation.surface: A citation about a wall built round the edge of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two letters turn up twice, once meaning 'about' (as in business letters) and once as the edges of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference is a passage cited from another work, the same as a quotation used to support a point.

clue.text: Win back heart of warrior queen, battling with orc

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter is kept
things in battle are thrown into confusion, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the fourth of seven letters
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fantasy tale: winning back a warrior queen's heart as she fights an orc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warrior queen' reads as one figure, but only the centre of warrior is used and queen joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconquer is to take control of a territory again after losing it, so the prefix re- makes it win back.

clue.text: Taken aback by private zoo banning drinks

indicators.note: taken from means drawn out of, so the letters are lifted straight from the words that follow
aback means backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, all of the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone is startled that a private zoo has banned drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' is a stock phrase for surprised, but here it is split into two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal slang for alcoholic liquor, so it stands for drinks in the sense of beer, wine and spirits.

clue.text: European married in style on vacation

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the word's inside goes and only its ends remain
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A European couple marries in grand style while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' reads as a honeymoon; it means emptying style out to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, a Scandinavian country in northern Europe, so is a European.

clue.text: Former partner entices diabolical being

indicators.note: something diabolical is dreadful and wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-partner lures in some devilish creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diabolical being' looks like a demon, but diabolical is the signal and being alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun means the state of existing, the fact of being alive or real, which is existence.

clue.text: Fellow leading a weird sect is thwarted by European powers

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, so the first piece heads the rest
something thwarted has an obstacle put in its way, so a letter blocks the middle

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for Fellow
taken as written
a cult is a sect with unorthodox beliefs
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A cult leader's bizarre sect is foiled by the great powers of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European powers' reads as nations, but European gives E and powers stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Faculties are mental or physical abilities such as sight or reason, so they are a person's powers.

clue.text: Hackers deliberately avoid young women

blocks.note: to cut someone is to snub them on purpose
lasses are girls, a northern British and Scottish word

explanation.surface: Computer hackers pointedly steer clear of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackers look like computer criminals; here they are things that hack, short curved swords.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short broad sword once used by sailors and pirates, a blade for hacking at an enemy.

clue.text: Mythical island cultivated grain and yams mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word's last letter is dropped
cultivated ground is turned over and worked, so these letters are churned up

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: A legendary isle where grain and yams are mostly farmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mythical island' reads as one place, like Atlantis, but island gives just I and Mythical is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mythical exists only in stories and legend, not in reality, so it is made up or imagined.

clue.text: Disease-ridden poor settle in east of Portugal

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked out of order
in an across clue east is to the right, so these letters come after

blocks.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sick, impoverished people make new homes in eastern Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle in' looks like the verb of the scene, but it is the fodder; 'east of' puts it after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent means carrying or spreading deadly plague, so a place full of pestilence is riddled with disease.

clue.text: Prevent upstanding husband rising to unfair criticism

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
rising in a down clue goes upward, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to prevent is to stop
H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upright husband stands up to block unjust attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' looks like praise for the husband, but it turns STOP upward; 'rising' does the same to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a cheap random attack, originally a shot at easy game, now a snide, unfair jibe at someone.

clue.text: Suspect characters in leathers had Yamahas

indicators.note: characters are letters, and those in the phrase that follows are lifted out as they stand

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, all of the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Dodgy-looking bikers in leather jackets riding Yamaha motorcycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect characters' reads as a pair of criminals, but characters belongs to the signal and Suspect alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady as an adjective means of doubtful honesty, just as suspect does when describing a dodgy person or deal.

clue.text: Bore accepted defeat

blocks.note: first meaning: produced, as a field bears crops
second meaning: gave in or surrendered

explanation.walkthrough: Bore looks like a dull person or the verb to tire; it is the past tense of bear, as in bore fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Yield means both to produce a crop or return and to give way in a contest, so the past tense fits each.

clue.text: Bird crossing extremely bare, mountainous region

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept
to cross something is to straddle it, so one piece spans the other

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bird flies over a stark, barren highland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely bare' reads as very bleak, but extremely means taking the two ends of bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is the high plateau region of Asia bordering the Himalayas, known as the roof of the world.

clue.text: Jostles politician boarding vehicle

indicators.note: a passenger boarding goes aboard and inside, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: a bus is a vehicle
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician shoves people aside as he gets on a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface picture of climbing aboard is also the mechanism: the politician gets inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump someone is to knock or push against them, so jostles and bumps are synonyms describing shoving in a crowd.

clue.text: Breaking cover, detective follows home waste collector?

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this piece is placed second
breaking into something means getting inside it, so letters split it open

blocks.note: a drape is a curtain or covering cloth
someone who is home is in
a PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A detective emerges from hiding to tail a rubbish collector home.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'Breaking' from 'cover', hiding that they are signal and container word. The question mark marks a playful definition: a drainpipe gathers waste water.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainpipe carries rainwater and waste water away from a building, so it collects waste in a loose, playful sense.

clue.text: Sits daughter in position of power for draughts

indicators.note: to stand in the position of another is to take its place, so one letter swaps for another

blocks.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
D is the abbreviation for daughter
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A parent seats a daughter in a seat of authority, perhaps at a game of draughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Position of power' reads as a throne, but it means the place where P stands in POSES. Draughts is the British name for checkers, the misdirection here.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is an old word for a measured quantity of liquid medicine, so draughts are doses.

clue.text: Sort of orange scar on abdomen

blocks.note: first meaning: a seedless orange with a navel-like pit at one end
second meaning: the belly button, left where the umbilical cord was cut

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings are spelt NAVEL; the published grid gives NAVAL, and its fourth square is unchecked, so this looks like a slip in the printed solution.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button is the scar where the umbilical cord was attached, and an orange of this variety has a similar mark.

clue.text: Preparing mean sushi makes one more relatable

indicators.note: preparing food means chopping and mixing it, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef's rough-and-ready sushi shows they are ordinary like the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective about stingy sushi, but it simply supplies four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To humanise someone is to present them as an ordinary person with feelings, so others can identify and sympathise with them.

clue.text: Delicacy finally served after a cracking French wine

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept
after means coming later, so this piece is placed behind the rest
to crack something is to break into it, so one piece gets inside another

blocks.note: vin is the French word for wine
taken as written
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fine dish arrives at the end, after a first-rate French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' reads as British slang for excellent, describing the wine; it means A breaks into VIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an old word for an item of food, especially a choice or tasty one, so a delicacy.

clue.text: They throw things at horses and zebras occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the even-placed letter of the word
the second, fourth and sixth letters
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Unruly spectators hurl objects at horses and zebras at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters are taken from 'at', 'horses' and 'zebras' in turn, skipping 'and'. The answer also has a rude British slang meaning, which the setter is surely winking at.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosser is literally someone who tosses, hurling or flinging objects, so the plural means people who throw things.

clue.text: Dramatic piece editor put on first of six-page spread

indicators.note: the first of something is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
in an across clue one thing put on another comes after it

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a play is a piece of drama
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor runs a theatre feature across a six-page magazine spread.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is magazine layout, but 'page' is padding in the hyphenated word, and 'spread' is the definition, not the layout term.
explanation.definitionFit: Splayed means spread out or apart, as fingers or legs are when opened wide from a central point.
